text.text_excerpt: This wonderful gelato parlor just re-opened on Oak Street and serves *the best* gelato in New Orleans. Honestly, it tastes just like the stuff in Italia. I had blood orange and lemoncello. Both were amazing. The whole place was spotless. The owner was so nice too. Not to mention the decor... couldn't have done it better myself. Did they pay me to write this? Maybe they'll pay me in gelato. :P

After a nice lunch on a Thursday afternoon, a friend and I wandered down the street for some gelato. Actually, she wanted it, I didn't. When we walked in we couldn't help but get excited by how cute the decor was. Bright, colorful and outside seating, which is always a plus for me. I didn't even really want any when we went in, but when I saw (and tasted) the blood orange sorbetto, I just couldn't help myself. It was wonderful. I don't know about other people's customer service experience, but I had a great one. We were greeted when we came through the door and the lady seemed happy to allow us to try whatever we wanted. I even asked why it was that I could plow through a pint of ice crea...

it's humid , muggy and you have been walking for blocks , what do I want ? Gelato! There it was a beautiful sign !Gelato and it was open , too! on our way to eat at Jacques-Imo's we find this little gem. The place was empty and going to closed at 8pm! Don't the good people of NOLA want creamy cool yummy treats? I guess not but I did. I had a small (big portion ) of Panna Cota . Creamy with a sweet almost caramelish taste twisted throughout. The other flavors were very traditional and looked wonderful. I noticed pistachio, baccio, chocolate, and stracetella(?). We would have gone back in a second if it had been near where we were staying.
